label: Gable Roof
volunteer_identification_guide: Triangular pitched roof with two sloping sides terminating in a vertical gable wall at each end.

label: Hipped Roof
volunteer_identification_guide: Slopes downwards to walls on all four sides, forming an inclined ridge and diagonal hip junctions; highly wind-resistant.

label: Half-hipped / Jerkinhead Roof
volunteer_identification_guide: Gable roof whose upper apex is truncated by a small sloping hip plane; vernacular compromise providing gable ventilation and hip stability.

label: Skillion / Shed Roof (Single Slope)
volunteer_identification_guide: Single sloping roof plane leaning against higher wall or freestanding; standard for verandahs, lean-to kitchen extensions, and open sheds.

label: Curved / Bullnose Roof
volunteer_identification_guide: Roof sheeting curved outwards at eaves or verandah margin; popularised late Victorian and Edwardian periods using curved corrugated iron.

label: Monitor / Sawtooth Roof
volunteer_identification_guide: Roof with vertical glazed or louvred clerestory ridge windows providing natural daylighting and ventilation across large woolshed shearing floors.

label: Corrugated Galvanised Iron (CGI)
volunteer_identification_guide: Curved or fluted sheet iron; check under-lap for stamped brands (Lysaght Orb, Gospel Oak, Redcliffe Crown).

label: Wood Shingles (Split or Sawn)
volunteer_identification_guide: Small rectangular timber tiles nailed to closely spaced roof battens; split hardwood pre-1865; machine-sawn post-1865; often concealed under later CGI.

label: Split Timber Palings
volunteer_identification_guide: Longer split timber slabs (0.9 to 1.5m long) overlapping on steep pitch roofs; typical pioneer bush roof covering.

label: Stringybark / Sheet Bark
volunteer_identification_guide: Large sheets of Eucalyptus bark stripped from trees in sap season, flattened under weights, held in place by sapling ridge poles and wire.

label: Roofing Slate
volunteer_identification_guide: Thin split natural stone tiles (Welsh or local) secured with copper or iron nails; high status domestic and institutional roofs.

label: Marseilles Terracotta Tiles
volunteer_identification_guide: Interlocking terracotta tiles with stamped maker marks; imported from France 1889-1915; manufactured locally in Australia by Wunderlich after 1916.

label: Shingle Battens Visible in Roof Space
volunteer_identification_guide: Closely spaced light horizontal battens (c. 150-200mm apart) carrying nail holes or wood splinters; confirms roof was originally shingled before CGI re-roofing.

label: Bark Ridge Props / Sapling Purlins
volunteer_identification_guide: Rough pole rafters with remnant stringybark fibres or wire ties from early bark roof.

label: Straight Skillion Verandah
volunteer_identification_guide: Straight slope running downwards from main eaves or outer wall at continuous or slightly lower pitch.

label: Broken-back Verandah
volunteer_identification_guide: Pitch breaks into a distinctly shallower angle at the main wall line, continuing over verandah as a shallower slope.

label: Bullnose Curved Verandah
volunteer_identification_guide: Curved convex profile at outer edge of roof; classic late Victorian and Federation rural aesthetic.

label: Concave / Ogee Verandah
volunteer_identification_guide: Graceful upward hollow sweeping concave curve or S-shaped ogee curve; distinctive Georgian and early/mid Victorian profile.

label: Bush Pole Verandah Post
volunteer_identification_guide: Round, peeled hardwood sapling or tree trunk; vernacular bush aesthetic.

label: Square Plain Timber Post
volunteer_identification_guide: Rough-sawn or dressed square hardwood timber (typically 100x100mm) without moulding.

label: Chamfered Timber Post
volunteer_identification_guide: Dressed timber post with chamfered / bevelled edges terminating in stop-chamfers near head and base.

label: Turned Timber Post
volunteer_identification_guide: Decorative post shaped on a wood-turning lathe with classical baluster rings; late Victorian/Federation.

label: Cast Iron Fluted / Decorative Post
volunteer_identification_guide: Hollow cast-iron column with integral classical base and capitals, often bolted to stone kerb; may feature foundry name.

label: Brick Chimney (External Breast)
volunteer_identification_guide: Corbelled or plain brick stack projecting from external gable wall; note whether handmade or machine bricks.

label: Stone / Rubble Chimney Stack
volunteer_identification_guide: Massive masonry chimney built of fieldstone or coursed sandstone with wide open hearth.

label: Corrugated Iron Cased Chimney
volunteer_identification_guide: Vernacular chimney constructed of timber frame clad externally in flat or corrugated iron, lined with mud-mortar pugging to prevent fire.

label: Split Slab & Mud/Pug Chimney
volunteer_identification_guide: Primitive bush chimney built of heavy vertical slabs lined internally with stone and rammed pug/clay.

label: Mass Concrete / Flue Pipe
volunteer_identification_guide: Cast concrete hearth or steel/asbestos flue pipe; 20th century installation.
